reasons.C: Crothers' playful mock-grandeur and whimsical asides (gods above Troy, no wish to attend the inquest, coat-tails) with short deflating sentences among longer ones, genial rather than preachy; the second-person 'you' is the only drift.
reasons.A: Has the passage's first-person, mock-solemn irony ('study of Providence', 'instruments of destiny') and short flat sentences for the letdown, but the last paragraph slides into earnest sermon longer than Crothers would stay there.
reasons.D: Closest on raw sentence movement, clipped declaratives like the passage's 'He suddenly stops', but the tone is more modern and neat ('merely a near thing', 'one braces') and lacks Crothers' whimsical period humour.
reasons.B: Most openly moralising and aphoristic ('The tragedy is in the altitude', 'Hope may be a matter of descending'); it argues a thesis where Crothers hints lightly, and 'I hold my breath' and the hedged close read as generic essayist.
